\section[viḷikkū]{\ml{വിളിക്കൂ} (viḷikkū) — please call}

\label{lesson:ML-C121-call}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for please help, then the Malayalam for please stop.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{വിളിക്കൂ}}
\textbf{\ml{വിളിക്കൂ}} (\emph{viḷikkū}) — \textquotedblleft{}please call (someone)\textquotedblright{}, or \textquotedblleft{}please phone\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
The request when help is needed.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{viḷikkū}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{viḷikkū}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{viḷikkū}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for please help, then the Malayalam for please stop, then say \emph{viḷikkū} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{വിളിക്കൂ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Please call\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[ṭikkaṟṟŭ]{\ml{ടിക്കറ്റ്} (ṭikkaṟṟŭ) — a ticket}

\label{lesson:ML-C121-ticket}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for please stop, then the Malayalam for please call.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{ടിക്കറ്റ്}}
\textbf{\ml{ടിക്കറ്റ്}} (\emph{ṭikkaṟṟŭ}) — \textquotedblleft{}a ticket\textquotedblright{}, from English. \textbf{\ml{ഒരു} \ml{ടിക്കറ്റ്}} — \textquotedblleft{}one ticket\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
An English word in Malayalam clothes.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṭikkaṟṟŭ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṭikkaṟṟŭ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{oru ṭikkaṟṟŭ}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for please stop, then the Malayalam for please call, then say \emph{ṭikkaṟṟŭ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{ടിക്കറ്റ്} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A ticket\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[bas]{\ml{ബസ്} (bas) — a bus}

\label{lesson:ML-C121-bus}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for please call, then the Malayalam for a ticket.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{ബസ്}}
\textbf{\ml{ബസ്}} (\emph{bas}) — \textquotedblleft{}a bus\textquotedblright{}. The \textbf{\ml{ബ}} is the letter you wrote from \textbf{\ml{ബുധൻ}}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
The everyday way to travel.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bas}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bas}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{bas}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for please call, then the Malayalam for a ticket, then say \emph{bas} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{ബസ്} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A bus\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[sṟṟēṣan]{\ml{സ്റ്റേഷൻ} (sṟṟēṣan) — a station}

\label{lesson:ML-C121-station}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for a ticket, then the Malayalam for a bus.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{സ്റ്റേഷൻ}}
\textbf{\ml{സ്റ്റേഷൻ}} (\emph{sṟṟēṣan}) — \textquotedblleft{}a station\textquotedblright{}, from English. \textbf{\ml{സ്റ്റേഷൻ} \ml{എവിടെ}?} — \textquotedblleft{}where is the station?\textquotedblright{}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Where the train stops.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sṟṟēṣan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sṟṟēṣan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} ask \emph{sṟṟēṣan eviṭe?}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for a ticket, then the Malayalam for a bus, then say \emph{sṟṟēṣan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{സ്റ്റേഷൻ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A station\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[bhūpaṭaṁ]{\ml{ഭൂപടം} (bhūpaṭaṁ) — a map}

\label{lesson:ML-C121-map}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for a bus, then the Malayalam for a station.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{ഭൂപടം}}
\textbf{\ml{ഭൂപടം}} (\emph{bhūpaṭaṁ}) — \textquotedblleft{}a map\textquotedblright{}, literally \textquotedblleft{}earth picture\textquotedblright{}: \textbf{\ml{ഭൂ}} (\emph{bhū}), \textquotedblleft{}earth\textquotedblright{}, and \textbf{\ml{പടം}} (\emph{paṭaṁ}), \textquotedblleft{}picture\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Earth, drawn on paper.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bhūpaṭaṁ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{bhūpaṭaṁ kāṇikkū}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for a bus, then the Malayalam for a station, then say \emph{bhūpaṭaṁ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
